definition: A recursive transition network ("RTN") is a graph theoretical schematic used to represent the rules of a context-free grammar.
details: RTNs have application to programming languages, natural language and lexical analysis. Any sentence that is constructed according to the rules of an RTN is said to be "well-formed". The structural elements of a well-formed sentence may also be well-formed sentences by themselves, or they may be simpler structures. This is why RTNs are described as recursive.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. Boil it down and it is this: A recursive transition network ("RTN") is a graph theoretical schematic used to represent the rules of a context-free grammar. Here is why it matters: RTNs have application to programming languages, natural language and lexical analysis. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. That blueprint is Recursive transition network.
